vulnerabilities.description: claimFileProjection identifies URL-like raw values as schemes, but the later containment branch does not exclude scheme paths or scheme-shaped repoPath values. With repoPath https://host/repo and raw https://host/repo/private/secret.ts (or analogous file: roots), sameDialect and prefix checks succeed and return private/secret.ts instead of basename-only, violating deny-by-default behavior for URL-like and misconfigured-root inputs.

edgeCasesMissed: Never allow containment proof when either the raw path or configured repository root is URL/scheme-like; test matching and mismatched http, https, file, and one-letter-scheme roots.
Exercise URL-like roots with mixed separators, case changes, query/fragment suffixes, and percent-encoded separators to ensure only a sanitized basename can survive.
Test process interruption between multiple mirror appends and SQLite commit if crash consistency, rather than synchronous append-failure rollback alone, is part of the JSONL-as-truth guarantee.
Test graph.import's existing-bootstrap no-op against changed malformed claims/source files to document whether source revalidation is intentionally skipped.
Only five pure/non-network focused tests executed here; 31 server tests requiring startServer could not bind port 0 in the restricted environment.
topFinding: URL-like repository roots remain eligible for lexical containment, so a matching URL raw value can expose directory ancestry even though URL-like and misconfigured-root inputs must always fall back to basename-only.

impact.rationale: The remaining issue is a continuable path-redaction defect, not a crash or core workflow break. Graph import now canonicalizes before effects; all write calls enter rollbackable synchronous mirror transactions; import and TTL side effects/broadcasts are deferred or restored; invalid recovery and startup levels are rejected; invalid rows are filtered before snapshot pagination; encoded traversal is excluded from containment; and Windows metrics follow case-insensitive projection classification.
